title: Prevent a slow sync client from blocking state broadcasts to other clients
description:
Review: Astra adversarial review — performance.

## Source locations

- `server/server.go:59`
- `server/server.go:178-195`
- `go.mod:16`

## Evidence

Pinned velox v0.4.2 go/state.go:250-257 holds connMut and calls c.Version for each client. go/conn.go:60-64 Version takes sendVerMut; send at :178-184 holds that same mutex throughout transport I/O. Therefore the next global Push can block on a previous slow client send. Default WriteTimeout is 30 seconds. Application accepts defaults via SyncHandler and has no per-client isolation override.

## Reproduction / validation

Connect a healthy SSE client and another that stops reading, then generate enough state to block the slow socket. The next global Push waits on slow-client Version while holding the subscriber mutex, delaying subsequent broadcasts/new subscriptions until the write timeout. This is proven lock-path analysis; no socket saturation test was run against the live app.

## Impact

One slow or abandoned browser can delay realtime updates for healthy browsers for up to the default 30-second timeout and block subscription changes.

## Acceptance criteria

Upgrade/fix the transport so reading connection version never waits on network I/O and the global subscriber lock is not held across potentially blocking client operations. An isolated slow-reader test should keep a second healthy client receiving updates promptly and reclaim timed-out send goroutines.

## Confidence

high on lock-path mechanism; impact duration is code-derived, not yet benchmarked

## Completion evidence

Velox v0.12.1 (upgraded for #50) snapshots subscribers and releases the global subscriber mutex before scheduling per-client version/send work. Per-client serialization remains isolated rather than blocking global broadcasts/subscriptions. The application now bypasses outer gzip on /sync so Velox owns SSE gzip and can set actual socket write deadlines. Upgraded request logging to requestlog/v2 v2.0.4, whose Unwrap preserves those deadlines with --log too.

An actual socket test uses the full app handler with gzip and logging enabled, a multi-megabyte incompressible state, one healthy SSE reader and one TCP client with a 1024-byte receive buffer that never reads. Healthy progress arrives in 324.7 ms while the slow send is still blocked; a third selective subscriber connects promptly. The configured three-second test deadline removes the slow subscription and returns actual transport-send goroutine profiles to baseline zero before the test closes the slow socket. Production retains the existing 30-second write deadline.

Full server race suite, embedded Go build, generated types and whitespace checks pass. Live main-app browser remains connected and recovers from disconnect with exactly one v3 connection.
